title: Explain what value-type and reference-type assignment copy, including shared reference fields

rubric.point: Explains that struct assignment copies each field into a separate struct value; it does not recursively clone referenced objects.
Explains that changing copy.Weight affects only the copy, so original.Weight remains 12.
Explains that the copied Labels reference initially points to the same list, so adding urgent changes the list reachable through original.
Explains that replacing copy.Labels changes only that struct's reference field; original.Labels still contains fragile and urgent.

questions.model:
`copy = original` copies both field values into a separate struct value. `Weight` contains an integer, while `Labels` contains a reference; the list itself is not copied.

Changing `copy.Weight` affects only the copied integer field. Initially, both `Labels` fields refer to one list, so adding `"urgent"` mutates that shared list. Assigning a new list to `copy.Labels` then replaces only the reference stored in `copy`.

Finally, `original.Weight` is `12`, and `original.Labels` contains `"fragile"` and `"urgent"`.

rubric.point: Explains that second = first copies the object reference, so both variables initially refer to the same Meter instance.
Explains that second.Reading = 15 changes a field on the shared instance, so first observes 15 despite the field being an integer.
Explains that assigning a new Meter replaces only second's reference; first still reaches the original instance with reading 15, while second reaches the new instance with reading 30.

questions.model:
`second = first` copies the reference to the `Meter`, so both variables initially reach the same instance. Its integer field has not been copied into a separate object. Changing `second.Reading` therefore changes the shared instance, and `first.Reading` becomes `15`.

The final assignment replaces the reference held by `second` with a reference to a new instance. It does not change `first` or the original instance. Finally, `first.Reading` is `15` and `second.Reading` is `30`.
